statement: The system shall allow a customer to initiate a laundry session for a specific machine by scanning a QR code located on that machine.
rationale: Provides a quick, frictionless way for customers to select a machine and begin the payment process without manual entry.

source.excerpt: We want to let customers walk in, scan a QR code on any machine, pay from their phone, and get notified when their cycle is done.
Every machine has a QR code.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer has the SpinCycle application open
acceptance_criteria.when: they scan a valid QR code on a laundry machine
acceptance_criteria.then: the application navigates to the control screen for that specific machine.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user does not have the app installed
acceptance_criteria.when: they scan a valid QR code on a laundry machine using their phone's native camera app
acceptance_criteria.then: they are directed to the Progressive Web App (PWA) to continue the process.

statement: The system shall allow customers to pay for laundry cycles using a digital payment method within the application.
rationale: Core functionality to enable a cashless laundromat, which reduces owner overhead and solves issues like coin jams.

source.excerpt: pay from their phone
Going cashless would be huge.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer has selected a machine and a cycle type
acceptance_criteria.when: they provide valid payment information and confirm the transaction
acceptance_criteria.then: the payment is successfully processed and the machine is commanded to start.

statement: The system shall send a push notification to the customer's device when their laundry cycle is complete.
rationale: Improves customer experience by allowing them to leave the premises without worrying about when to return for their laundry.

source.excerpt: and get notified when their cycle is done.
When the cycle ends, they get a push notification saying "Your laundry is done at Machine W-07."

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer has a cycle running
acceptance_criteria.when: the machine signals the end of the cycle
acceptance_criteria.then: the customer receives a push notification indicating the cycle is complete and which machine it was.

statement: The system shall provide a web-based dashboard for laundromat owners and staff.
rationale: Provides a centralized interface for owners to manage their business, view analytics, and monitor operations.

source.excerpt: On the owner side, Dana and folks like her need a dashboard showing real-time machine status, revenue reports, and maintenance alerts.

acceptance_criteria.given: an authorized owner or staff member has valid credentials
acceptance_criteria.when: they navigate to the dashboard URL and log in
acceptance_criteria.then: they are presented with the main dashboard interface.

statement: The owner dashboard shall display the real-time status of all machines in a selected location.
rationale: Gives owners immediate visibility into their floor operations without needing to be physically present.

source.excerpt: ...a dashboard showing real-time machine status...
A live floor map — same as the customer but with more detail.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing their location dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine becomes idle
acceptance_criteria.then: the dashboard updates to show that machine's status as 'idle' within the defined latency threshold.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing their location dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: a customer starts a machine
acceptance_criteria.then: the dashboard updates to show that machine's status as 'running' and displays the remaining cycle time.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing their location dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine has a status of 'out of order'
acceptance_criteria.then: the dashboard updates to show that machine's status as 'out of order' within the defined latency threshold.

statement: The owner dashboard shall provide access to revenue reports.
rationale: Allows owners to track financial performance and make informed business decisions.

source.excerpt: ...revenue reports...
Revenue today versus yesterday versus same day last week.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner with financial permissions is logged into the dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: they navigate to the revenue reporting section
acceptance_criteria.then: they can view key metrics such as revenue for today, yesterday, and the same day last week.

statement: The owner dashboard shall display maintenance alerts for machines that have faulted.
rationale: Enables proactive maintenance, reducing machine downtime and costly repairs.

source.excerpt: ...maintenance alerts.
Alerts for machines that have faulted.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is logged into the dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine's IoT controller reports a fault code
acceptance_criteria.then: a maintenance alert for that machine is displayed on the dashboard.

statement: The system shall track and report the status of each machine, including 'idle', 'running', and 'out of order'.
rationale: This is a fundamental capability that underpins real-time maps for customers, dashboards for owners, and notifications.

source.excerpt: Each machine should report whether it's idle, running, or out of order.

acceptance_criteria.given: a machine is powered on and connected but not in a cycle
acceptance_criteria.when: the system receives a status update from its IoT controller
acceptance_criteria.then: the machine's status is recorded as 'idle'.

acceptance_criteria.given: a machine is in an active, paid cycle
acceptance_criteria.when: the system receives a status update from its IoT controller
acceptance_criteria.then: the machine's status is recorded as 'running'.

acceptance_criteria.given: a machine reports a critical fault or is manually flagged for maintenance
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes this event
acceptance_criteria.then: the machine's status is recorded as 'out of order'.

statement: The system's IoT controllers shall use the MQTT protocol to communicate status updates to the backend.
rationale: Defines the specific technology to be used for IoT communication, as determined by the technical team.

source.excerpt: They'll push status over MQTT every ten seconds.
the IoT boards publish to an MQTT broker.

statement: IoT controllers shall publish a status update at least every 10 seconds.
rationale: Ensures that the system has a reasonably fresh view of the machine state for real-time dashboards and applications.

source.excerpt: They'll push status over MQTT every ten seconds.

statement: The system shall use Stripe Connect for payment processing to handle fund settlement to individual laundromat owners.
rationale: Specifies the third-party payment provider and platform (Stripe Connect) to ensure correct routing of funds and simplify PCI compliance.

source.excerpt: For payments we plan to integrate Stripe Connect so each laundromat location is a connected account and funds settle directly to the owner.

statement: The system shall provide a Progressive Web App (PWA) to allow customers to use the service without installing a native mobile application.
rationale: Lowers the barrier to entry for new or infrequent customers who may not want to install a full application.

source.excerpt: They open the SpinCycle app — or a progressive web app if they don't want to install anything.
Scanning it opens the PWA, which handles one-time guest checkout.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user scans a machine's QR code without the native app installed
acceptance_criteria.when: they are redirected to the PWA in their mobile browser
acceptance_criteria.then: they can complete a payment and start a machine cycle as a guest.

statement: The customer application shall display a visual map of the laundromat, color-coding machines by status: green for available, yellow for in-use, and red for out-of-order.
rationale: Provides customers with an at-a-glance view of machine availability, improving their experience and reducing time spent searching for a free machine.

source.excerpt: They see a map of the location showing which machines are available in green, in-use in yellow, and out-of-order in red.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer is viewing the laundromat map
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine has a status of 'idle'
acceptance_criteria.then: it is displayed with a green color indicator.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer is viewing the laundromat map
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine has a status of 'running'
acceptance_criteria.then: it is displayed with a yellow color indicator.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer is viewing the laundromat map
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine has a status of 'out of order'
acceptance_criteria.then: it is displayed with a red color indicator.

statement: The system shall physically start a machine's cycle within 5 seconds of a successful payment confirmation.
rationale: Ensures a responsive and satisfactory user experience, giving the customer immediate feedback that their payment was successful.

source.excerpt: The machine starts within five seconds of payment confirmation.
Payment confirmation to machine start within five seconds — that's end to end including Stripe's authorization round trip.

metric.condition: From successful payment API response to machine start command being sent.

statement: The system shall allow customers to complete a transaction as a guest without creating an account.
rationale: Reduces friction for first-time or infrequent users.

source.excerpt: Scanning it opens the PWA, which handles one-time guest checkout.
No account required.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new customer has selected a machine and cycle
acceptance_criteria.when: they proceed to payment
acceptance_criteria.then: they are able to complete the transaction by providing only payment details, without being forced to create a password or user profile.

statement: The system shall provide an optional customer account that allows access to features like loyalty points.
rationale: Encourages customer retention and provides a foundation for personalized features.

source.excerpt: if they do create an account they can earn loyalty points.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer is using the application
acceptance_criteria.when: they choose to sign up for an account
acceptance_criteria.then: they can create a persistent profile to track their history and loyalty status.

statement: The system shall implement a loyalty program for registered customers.
rationale: Incentivizes repeat business and increases customer lifetime value.

source.excerpt: if they do create an account they can earn loyalty points.

acceptance_criteria.given: a registered customer completes a paid transaction
acceptance_criteria.when: the payment is successfully processed
acceptance_criteria.then: the corresponding number of loyalty points are added to their account.

acceptance_criteria.given: a registered customer has accumulated enough points for a reward
acceptance_criteria.when: they choose to redeem the reward on a qualifying transaction
acceptance_criteria.then: the reward is applied and their point balance is debited accordingly.

statement: Registered customers shall earn one loyalty point for every full dollar spent (e.g., a $3.50 purchase earns 3 points), and can redeem 100 points for a free standard wash.
rationale: Defines the specific earn and burn rates for the loyalty program, clarifying that points are awarded by flooring the dollar amount of the transaction.

source.excerpt: Simple tier system. Every dollar spent earns one point.
At a hundred points you get a free standard wash — roughly a ten-percent rebate.
Assumed that points are awarded only for whole dollars spent (i.e., a $3.50 purchase earns 3 points) to resolve ambiguity in the transcript.

statement: The system shall offer a monthly subscription plan ('Spin Pass') for customers.
rationale: Creates a predictable, recurring revenue stream for laundromat owners and offers value to frequent customers.

source.excerpt: We want a "Spin Pass" monthly subscription option too: twenty-five dollars a month for unlimited standard washes at a single location.
I love the subscription idea.

acceptance_criteria.given: a registered customer is not a subscriber
acceptance_criteria.when: they navigate to the subscription section and complete the sign-up process
acceptance_criteria.then: their account is marked as an active 'Spin Pass' subscriber and they are billed the monthly fee.

acceptance_criteria.given: an active 'Spin Pass' subscriber selects a standard wash
acceptance_criteria.when: they proceed to checkout
acceptance_criteria.then: the price is displayed as $0 and they can start the machine without a new charge.

statement: The 'Spin Pass' subscription shall provide unlimited standard washes at a single, designated location for a monthly fee of $25.
rationale: Defines the specific terms, benefits, and price of the subscription plan.

source.excerpt: twenty-five dollars a month for unlimited standard washes at a single location.

statement: 'Spin Pass' subscribers shall receive a 50% discount on premium cycle types.
rationale: Adds value to the subscription and encourages upselling to higher-margin cycles.

source.excerpt: Premium cycles like sanitize or extra-large would be discounted fifty percent for subscribers.

statement: The system shall send a reminder notification to a customer if their completed laundry has not been collected within 5 minutes of the cycle finishing.
rationale: Helps improve machine turnover by gently nudging customers to retrieve their items, benefiting other waiting customers.

source.excerpt: Five minutes after a cycle ends, if the door hasn't been opened, send the customer a reminder.
The IoT board can detect door-open events, so we'll know when someone actually unloads.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's laundry cycle has been complete for 5 minutes
acceptance_criteria.when: the system has not detected a 'door-open' event for that machine
acceptance_criteria.then: a reminder push notification is sent to the customer.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's laundry cycle has been complete for 4 minutes
acceptance_criteria.when: the customer opens the machine door
acceptance_criteria.then: no reminder notification is sent.

statement: The system shall support applying an idle fee for laundry not collected after a pre-defined duration has passed since the cycle's completion.
rationale: Strongly incentivizes customers to free up machines, maximizing throughput for the laundromat owner.

source.excerpt: After fifteen minutes, start a small idle fee — maybe twenty-five cents per minute — so people have an incentive to come get their stuff.

acceptance_criteria.given: the idle fee feature is enabled for a location and set to a 15-minute grace period
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine has been idle with a completed cycle for 15 minutes and 1 second without the door being opened
acceptance_criteria.then: the system begins to accrue an idle fee on the customer's account.

acceptance_criteria.given: an idle fee is accruing for a customer
acceptance_criteria.when: the customer opens the machine door
acceptance_criteria.then: the system stops accruing the fee and finalizes the total charge.

acceptance_criteria.given: an idle fee is accruing at $0.25/min
acceptance_criteria.when: the customer opens the machine door after 16 minutes and 30 seconds have passed since the cycle completed (1.5 fee-eligible minutes)
acceptance_criteria.then: the system finalizes the total charge for 2 full minutes of idle time, for a total of $0.50.

statement: Idle fees shall be billed in full-minute increments, where any partial minute incurs the full per-minute charge (e.g., 90 seconds of idle time is billed as 2 minutes). The rate shall be configurable by the owner, with a suggested default of $0.25 per minute.
rationale: Defines the billing logic and default rate for the idle fee feature, ensuring transparency for the customer.

source.excerpt: maybe twenty-five cents per minute
We should probably bill in full-minute increments and clearly disclose that.

statement: The idle fee feature shall be configurable (enabled/disabled) on a per-location basis by the laundromat owner.
rationale: Provides flexibility for owners who may want different policies for different locations or may wish to opt out of this feature entirely.

source.excerpt: I'd say we build the notifications and the idle-fee logic but keep the fee togglable per location.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing the settings for one of their locations in the dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: they toggle the 'Enable Idle Fee' setting to OFF
acceptance_criteria.then: customers at that location will no longer accrue idle fees.

statement: The owner dashboard shall include a maintenance log for each machine.
rationale: Allows technicians to track repair history, record notes, and manage the status of machines under repair.

source.excerpt: And a maintenance log where my technician can mark a machine as "under repair" and add notes.

acceptance_criteria.given: an authorized staff member is viewing a machine's details in the dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: they add a new log entry with notes and set the status to 'under repair'
acceptance_criteria.then: the machine's status is updated to 'out of order' and the entry is saved in the machine's history.

statement: The system shall implement role-based access control (RBAC) for the owner dashboard to restrict access to data and functionality based on user role.
rationale: Ensures that staff members only have access to the information and tools necessary for their jobs, protecting sensitive financial data.

source.excerpt: Each location has its own staff, so role-based access is important
my floor attendants should see machine status but not revenue numbers.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user with the 'Attendant' role is logged in
acceptance_criteria.when: they attempt to access the revenue analytics page
acceptance_criteria.then: access is denied.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user with the 'Owner' role is logged in
acceptance_criteria.when: they access the revenue analytics page
acceptance_criteria.then: the page is displayed with all data.

statement: The 'Owner' role shall have full access to all data and functionality for all locations associated with their account, including aggregate views.
rationale: Defines the permissions for the top-level user role.

source.excerpt: Owner sees everything.
I need to switch between them or see an aggregate view.

statement: The 'Manager' role shall have full access to all data and functionality, but only for their specifically assigned location(s).
rationale: Defines the permissions for a location-specific management role.

source.excerpt: Manager sees everything for their assigned location.

statement: The 'Attendant' role shall be able to view machine status and change a machine's status to 'out of order' by creating a maintenance log entry, but shall have no access to financial data.
rationale: Defines the permissions for a limited, operational-focused role, empowering floor staff to immediately prevent customers from using a broken machine.

source.excerpt: Attendant sees machine status and can flag maintenance issues but no financial data.
My floor staff needs the ability to put a machine into an 'out of order' state themselves to prevent customers from using a broken machine.

statement: The system shall allow customers to register and authenticate using an email address and password.
rationale: Provides a traditional, standard method for account creation and login.

source.excerpt: For customers, email plus password or social login — Google and Apple.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new user provides a valid email and password
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the registration form
acceptance_criteria.then: an account is created and they are logged in.

statement: The system shall allow customers to register and authenticate using their Google account (social login).
rationale: Offers a convenient, low-friction authentication method for a large segment of users.

source.excerpt: For customers, email plus password or social login — Google and Apple.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new user is on the login screen
acceptance_criteria.when: they click 'Sign in with Google' and successfully authenticate with Google
acceptance_criteria.then: a SpinCycle account is created for them and they are logged into the application.

statement: The system shall allow customers to register and authenticate using their Apple ID (social login).
rationale: Offers a convenient, low-friction, and privacy-focused authentication method for users in the Apple ecosystem.

source.excerpt: For customers, email plus password or social login — Google and Apple.

acceptance_criteria.given: a new user is on the login screen on an Apple device
acceptance_criteria.when: they tap 'Sign in with Apple' and successfully authenticate with Apple
acceptance_criteria.then: a SpinCycle account is created for them and they are logged into the application.

statement: The system shall enforce Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) two-factor authentication (2FA) for all owner dashboard users.
rationale: Enhances the security of owner and staff accounts, which have access to sensitive financial and operational data.

source.excerpt: For the owner dashboard we want to enforce two-factor authentication, probably TOTP-based.

acceptance_criteria.given: a dashboard user has entered their correct username and password
acceptance_criteria.when: they are prompted for a 2FA code
acceptance_criteria.then: they must enter a valid code from their TOTP authenticator app to complete the login.

statement: The platform shall collect a 7% service fee from each transaction, with the remainder settling to the laundromat owner's connected account.
rationale: Defines the core business model for the SpinCycle platform.

source.excerpt: The platform takes a seven-percent service fee off each transaction, and the remainder settles to the laundromat's connected Stripe account.

statement: Payouts of collected funds to laundromat owners shall occur on a two-day rolling basis.
rationale: Sets the expectation for how quickly owners will receive their revenue.

source.excerpt: Payouts happen on a two-day rolling basis.

statement: The system shall allow customers to request a refund for a transaction through the application.
rationale: Provides a self-service method for customers to report issues like machine malfunctions and initiate a resolution process.

source.excerpt: If a machine malfunctions mid-cycle, the customer should be able to request a refund from the app.

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer is viewing their transaction history
acceptance_criteria.when: they select a transaction and tap the 'Request Refund' option
acceptance_criteria.then: a refund request is created and placed in a 'pending' state for manager review.

statement: The owner dashboard shall allow authorized users (Manager or Owner) to approve or deny pending refund requests.
rationale: Gives owners control over the refund process, allowing them to validate requests before funds are returned.

source.excerpt: It goes into a pending state, the location manager approves or denies, and then we process it through Stripe.

acceptance_criteria.given: a manager is viewing a pending refund request
acceptance_criteria.when: they click 'Approve'
acceptance_criteria.then: the refund is processed via the payment gateway and the request status is updated to 'Approved'.

acceptance_criteria.given: a manager is viewing a pending refund request
acceptance_criteria.when: they click 'Deny'
acceptance_criteria.then: the request status is updated to 'Denied' and no refund is issued.

statement: The IoT controllers must be able to buffer at least 4 hours of status events to handle network connectivity outages.
rationale: Ensures data integrity and accurate reporting by preventing data loss during temporary internet disruptions at the laundromat.

source.excerpt: The boards have a small flash buffer — about four hours of events.

metric.condition: Buffering of machine status events during network outage.

statement: The system shall allow customers to start machines during an internet outage.
rationale: Provides maximum uptime and business continuity for the laundromat owner.

source.excerpt: offline machine start is a post-launch feature.

statement: The customer-facing application (native and PWA) shall be compliant with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA.
rationale: Ensures the application is usable by people with a wide range of disabilities, including visual and motor impairments.

source.excerpt: The app needs to meet WCAG 2.1 AA.

statement: The customer-facing application shall support English and Spanish languages.
rationale: Serves a broader customer base in diverse neighborhoods.

source.excerpt: We serve diverse neighborhoods — English and Spanish at launch, with a localization framework so adding languages later is just a translation file.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user's device is set to Spanish
acceptance_criteria.when: they open the SpinCycle application
acceptance_criteria.then: all UI text is displayed in Spanish.

acceptance_criteria.given: a user's device is set to English
acceptance_criteria.when: they open the SpinCycle application
acceptance_criteria.then: all UI text is displayed in English.

statement: Machine status changes must be reflected in the customer and owner applications within 2 seconds of the corresponding event being published by the IoT device.
rationale: Ensures that the information presented to users is timely and accurate, fostering trust in the system.

source.excerpt: Machine status updates should reflect in the app within two seconds of the MQTT event.

metric.condition: p95 of all status updates from MQTT publish to client UI render.

statement: The owner dashboard shall achieve initial data load in under 3 seconds.
rationale: Provides a responsive and efficient user experience for owners managing their business.

source.excerpt: The dashboard should load initial data in under three seconds on a standard broadband connection.

metric.condition: On a standard broadband connection (e.g., 25 Mbps).

statement: The public-facing APIs shall achieve a monthly uptime of at least 99.9%.
rationale: Ensures high availability and reliability for the service, which is critical for both customer-facing operations and payment processing.

source.excerpt: We're targeting ninety-nine-point-nine percent uptime for the API.

statement: The system shall allow customers to join a virtual waitlist for a specific type of machine (e.g., front-load washer) when none are available.
rationale: Improves customer experience during peak hours by allowing them to queue without physically waiting in the laundromat.

source.excerpt: "Machine available" — if all machines are busy, a customer can join a virtual waitlist and get notified when one frees up.
The waitlist thing would be great.

acceptance_criteria.given: all machines of a certain type are currently in use
acceptance_criteria.when: a customer selects that machine type and taps 'Notify me'
acceptance_criteria.then: they are added to the end of the virtual waitlist for that machine type.

acceptance_criteria.given: a machine becomes available and its waitlist is processed
acceptance_criteria.when: the last notified user's 5-minute claim window expires without them starting a cycle
acceptance_criteria.then: the machine's status becomes generally available to all customers on the map.

statement: The system shall notify the first customer in a waitlist queue via push notification when a matching machine becomes available.
rationale: Closes the loop on the waitlist feature, making it useful for the customer.

source.excerpt: When any front-load washer at that location becomes idle, the first person in the queue gets a push notification...

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer is first in the waitlist for a front-load washer
acceptance_criteria.when: a front-load washer's status changes to 'idle'
acceptance_criteria.then: that customer receives a push notification and their claim timer begins.

statement: A customer notified from the waitlist shall have 5 minutes to start a cycle on an available machine. If they do not claim a machine in time, their spot is forfeited and the next person in the queue is notified. If there are no more users in the queue, the machine becomes generally available.
rationale: Ensures the waitlist moves efficiently and doesn't leave machines idle for extended periods.

source.excerpt: ...and has five minutes to start a cycle. If they don't, it moves to the next person.

statement: All financial transaction data must be retained for a minimum of 7 years.
rationale: Complies with standard financial and tax auditing requirements.

source.excerpt: Transaction data kept for seven years for tax purposes.

statement: Raw machine telemetry event data shall be purged after 90 days, but daily aggregated telemetry data shall be retained indefinitely.
rationale: Manages data storage costs by retaining only valuable long-term data while discarding granular, short-term data.

source.excerpt: Machine telemetry — raw events can be purged after ninety days, but daily aggregates kept indefinitely for trend analysis.

statement: All network traffic between clients (app, dashboard, IoT) and backend servers must be encrypted using TLS 1.3.
rationale: Ensures data is secure in transit, protecting against eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks.

source.excerpt: All traffic TLS 1.3.

statement: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) must be encrypted at rest using AES-256.
rationale: Protects sensitive customer data stored in the database from unauthorized access.

source.excerpt: PII encrypted at rest — AES-256.

statement: The system shall allow authorized users to reserve a group of specific machines for a defined time window in a single operation.
rationale: Accommodates corporate or high-value clients who require guaranteed availability for multiple machines at specific times, streamlining the booking process for staff.

source.excerpt: They'd love to reserve three washers from six to eight AM.
I said I need to 'reserve three washers from six to eight AM' for my corporate clients, implying a single action for a group of machines.
Resolve the critic issue by adopting the current implementation draft for REQ-053.

acceptance_criteria.given: a laundromat manager is logged into the dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: they select three specific washers, a date, and a time window from 6 AM to 8 AM and create a group reservation
acceptance_criteria.then: the system records the reservation for all three selected machines.

statement: Reserved machines shall be blocked from general availability in the customer application during their reservation window.
rationale: Ensures that reservations are honored and reserved machines are not used by other customers.

source.excerpt: It should block those machines from general availability during that window.

acceptance_criteria.given: a machine is reserved from 6 AM to 8 AM
acceptance_criteria.when: a general customer views the machine map at 7 AM
acceptance_criteria.then: the reserved machine is shown as unavailable (e.g., greyed out or with a 'Reserved' status).

statement: A 50% cancellation fee shall be charged if a machine reservation is cancelled less than two hours before its scheduled start time, based on a yet-to-be-defined reservation cost.
rationale: Compensates the owner for lost revenue opportunity from late cancellations. The basis for calculating the fee (e.g., estimated cycle costs, flat fee) is not yet defined.

source.excerpt: Reservations with a configurable cancellation policy — cancel up to two hours before the window, otherwise you're charged fifty percent.
Resolve the critic issue by adopting the current implementation draft for REQ-055.

statement: The owner dashboard shall provide a revenue analytics page with visualizations.
rationale: Allows owners to understand business trends and performance at a deeper level than simple reports.

source.excerpt: We also want a revenue analytics page: revenue per machine, per cycle type, peak hours heatmap, and average turnaround time.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing the revenue analytics page
acceptance_criteria.when: they select the 'Peak Hours Heatmap' view
acceptance_criteria.then: a visual chart is displayed showing the busiest days and times for their location.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing the revenue analytics page
acceptance_criteria.when: they select the 'Revenue by Machine' view
acceptance_criteria.then: a report or chart is displayed showing the total revenue generated by each individual machine over the selected time period.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing the revenue analytics page
acceptance_criteria.when: they select the 'Revenue by Cycle Type' view
acceptance_criteria.then: a report or chart is displayed showing the total revenue generated by each cycle type over the selected time period.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing the revenue analytics page
acceptance_criteria.when: they view the summary metrics
acceptance_criteria.then: the average machine turnaround time for the selected period is displayed.

statement: The system shall allow owners to export revenue and transaction data to a CSV file.
rationale: Facilitates offline analysis and integration with external accounting software.

source.excerpt: Exportable to CSV for their accountants.
I need daily transaction reports for my bookkeeper.

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is viewing a revenue report
acceptance_criteria.when: they click the 'Export to CSV' button
acceptance_criteria.then: a CSV file containing the data from the current report view is downloaded to their computer.

statement: The customer API must be rate-limited to 100 requests per minute per user.
rationale: Prevents system abuse and ensures fair resource allocation among users.

source.excerpt: API rate limiting to prevent abuse: a hundred requests per minute per user for the customer API, higher limits for dashboard users.

statement: The system shall allow administrators to define different laundry cycle types (e.g., Normal, Delicate, Heavy-Duty) with associated prices and durations.
rationale: This is a necessary prerequisite for allowing customers to choose a cycle and be charged correctly.

source.excerpt: Inferred from the statement: 'They tap an available machine, pick a wash cycle — normal, delicate, heavy-duty — and confirm payment.'

statement: The system shall allow a laundromat owner to send promotional notifications to registered customers of a specific location.
rationale: Enables owners to run marketing campaigns and drive traffic during off-peak hours, increasing revenue.

source.excerpt: Promotional notifications — the owner can push a deal like "free dry with every wash this Thursday."

acceptance_criteria.given: an owner is logged into the dashboard
acceptance_criteria.when: they compose a promotional message and send it to a specific location's customers
acceptance_criteria.then: registered customers who have opted into notifications for that location receive the promotional push notification.

statement: The system shall generate a maintenance alert visible within the owner dashboard when a machine reports a fault.
rationale: Ensures maintenance issues are addressed promptly by notifying staff via the primary management tool, reducing machine downtime.

source.excerpt: And maintenance alerts to staff when a machine reports a fault code.

acceptance_criteria.given: a machine's IoT controller publishes a fault code
acceptance_criteria.when: the system processes the event
acceptance_criteria.then: a maintenance alert is generated and associated with the machine and its location.

acceptance_criteria.given: an authorized staff member is logged into the dashboard for a specific location
acceptance_criteria.when: a machine at their location reports a fault
acceptance_criteria.then: a persistent, visible alert appears in the dashboard UI until it is acknowledged.

statement: The system backend shall maintain a local payment ledger to ensure the owner dashboard can display revenue data independently of the payment processor's API latency.
rationale: Guarantees a responsive and available revenue dashboard for owners, even if the primary payment provider's reporting API is slow or temporarily unavailable.

source.excerpt: We'll store a payment ledger locally so the dashboard can show revenue even if Stripe's reporting API is slow.

statement: The system API must support at least 500 concurrent users per location without performance degradation.
rationale: Ensures the system remains stable and responsive during peak usage times at busy laundromat locations.

source.excerpt: Load testing to verify the API handles at least five hundred concurrent users per location without degradation.

metric.condition: While maintaining API response times under defined thresholds (e.g., p95 < 500ms).
